topline.text: CST's Annual Conference wrapped up today in Birmingham, with trust leaders focused on how the Schools White Paper and SEND reforms land in practice for mainstream inclusion.
topline.action: Worth checking CST's post-event output if your trust was represented.

topline.text: Today (16 Oct) employers can formally start consulting staff on pay policies for the 3.5% 2026-27 teacher pay award - the Pay Order itself still has to clear Parliament.
A quieter day otherwise: no major new England-wide SEND or inclusion announcements since yesterday's Ofsted leadership story, which remains unresolved.

diary.text: Employers in England can begin consulting staff on updated pay policies for the 2026-27 teacher pay award.
Sheffield City Council finance and performance committee votes on £602k funding for the Firth Park Academy SEND-places expansion.

sections.heading: CST Annual Conference: trusts on SEND reform

items.body: The Confederation of School Trusts' Annual Conference ran 15-16 October at Birmingham's ICC, with sessions on how sector and civic leaders respond to the Schools White Paper and SEND reforms - including a breakout on 'Inclusive by design: creating environments where all learners thrive'.

From 16 October, employers can consult staff on pay policies reflecting the accepted 3.5% uplift for 2026-27 (5% at the bottom of the unqualified range), backdated to 1 September. The Pay Order itself still needs to clear its parliamentary praying period before arrears follow.

box.label: Jargon-buster - OAIP
box.intro: Cropping up at this week's CST conference on SEND reform:
box.text: Ordinarily Available Inclusive Practice - the support mainstream schools should provide without needing an EHCP, now being folded into local 'ordinarily available provision' guidance as part of the wider SEND reforms.
